title: The Last Spire Again
premise: Yara Lockridge has spent her life running contraband through the Thornfell passes for the Lockridge Guild, now down to its last three members. When prayers to the old gods begin to be answered, Yara learns her grandmother's dying bargain sold Yara's soul to the Undercourt beneath the mountain — the price that kept the guild's roads open for a generation. To reclaim it, she must descend into the court of the usurper-god Vaskal, guided by a disgraced priest named Cael who once served the god he now hunts. As Vaskal's armies march toward the free cities, Yara discovers the stolen soul is not only hers: it is the keystone of the old gods' return, and freeing it will either restore them or unmake the mountains entirely. She pays the price of survival by giving up the guild's last secret — the true road through Thornfell — and in the end chooses love over duty, binding her soul freely to Cael and the waking gods rather than to any court, mortal or divine.
about_author: Wren Iversen is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through the Carpathian passes before turning to fantasy. They write stories about stubborn people, old bargains, and the geography of debts.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Yara POV. She runs a final smuggling route through the Thornfells as winter closes, carrying medicine to a village that prays to gods everyone knows are dead. The medicine works impossibly well. Emotional beat: unease — the world is quietly changing, and Yara's practical certainty begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Guild of Three
chapters.summary: Yara POV. She returns to the guildhall to find only her grandmother Marette and old Brenn left, the ledgers full of debts no one can collect. Marette coughs blood and mutters about a bargain coming due. Emotional beat: grief and stubborn pride in a dying inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Prayers Bought
chapters.summary: Yara POV. A stranger, the defrocked priest Cael, arrives seeking passage and reveals the truth: Marette sold Yara's soul to the Undercourt to seal the guild's roads, and now the old gods stir because the bargain is failing. Emotional beat: betrayal — Yara learns her whole life was collateral.

chapters.title: Marette's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marette POV, in her final days. She recounts the famine winter when she made the bargain with Vaskal's herald, and what the guild's roads cost. She dies at dawn, her last word Yara's name. Emotional beat: tragic love, a grandmother's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Road Nobody Sells
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Refusing to grieve, Yara decides to descend into the Undercourt and steal her soul back, forcing Cael to guide her to a gate only priests remember. Emotional beat: cold resolve; love against duty begins as duty to the dead.

chapters.title: Vaskal's Vanguard
chapters.summary: Brenn POV, left behind. The usurper's armies appear in the lowlands, burning shrines of the old gods and conscripting free-city border towns. Brenn sends warning up the pass. Emotional beat: dread; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Hollow Chapel
chapters.summary: Yara POV. She and Cael find the descent gate in a ruined chapel; Cael confesses he once served Vaskal and was cast out for mercy. Their first real argument — and first moment of trust. Emotional beat: wary intimacy between two people defined by old failures.

chapters.title: Down the Rootways
chapters.summary: Yara POV. They descend through root-tunnels where the mountain itself seems half-asleep, encountering a river that answers questions and stones that remember names. Yara realizes the old gods aren't returning — they're being woken. Emotional beat: wonder braided with fear.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Cael POV. At the Undercourt's threshold, a gatekeeper demands a true name as toll. Cael offers his own; Yara refuses to let him, and they trick the gate with a name Marette left hidden in the ledger. Emotional beat: Yara chooses Cael over the easy path — love against duty, first bloom.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Yara POV. They enter Vaskal's court, a mirrored inversion of the guildhall, where souls are kept as coin and the usurper holds court over sleeping god-flesh. Yara sees her soul: a small bright lamp in a vault of thousands. Emotional beat: horror and recognition.

chapters.title: An Audience of Debts
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Brought before Vaskal, she learns the bargain's true terms: her soul is the keystone that will let Vaskal devour the waking old gods and rule the mountains forever. He offers her a place at his right hand. Emotional beat: temptation — survival offered at the price of everyone else.

chapters.title: The Priest's Confession
chapters.summary: Cael POV. Imprisoned, Cael tells Yara the rest: he helped Vaskal seal the old gods the first time, and his mercy was not exile but escape. He believes he deserves whatever comes. Emotional beat: shame met by Yara's fierce, undeserved forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Vault of Lamps
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Using smuggler's craft — locks, ledgers, mislabeled cargo — Yara breaks into the soul-vault and finds her lamp is fused to thousands of others: freeing hers frees them all, or destroys them. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and unbearable.

chapters.title: What Brenn Carried Down
chapters.summary: Brenn POV. Wounded and half-dead, Brenn reaches the court bearing Marette's ledger and the guild's last secret: the true road through Thornfell, the one thing Vaskal's armies lack. Emotional beat: loyalty outlasting death; inheritance passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Vaskal offers to spare the free cities if Yara surrenders her soul willingly. She refuses — and Brenn burns the ledger page holding the true road, dying to keep it from the court. Emotional beat: fury and grief; the cost of refusal made flesh.

chapters.title: Riot of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Cael POV. Yara shatters the vault; the freed souls flood the court, and the sleeping god-flesh beneath the mountain begins to wake in agony and joy. Cael sings the old litany to gentle them, redeeming his betrayal. Emotional beat: chaos transfigured into grace.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Fall
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Vaskal, unmade by the waking gods, tries to drag Yara down with him; Cael takes the blow meant for her. The court collapses as the mountain exhales. Emotional beat: climax — love paid in blood, duty and love finally the same choice.

chapters.title: The Waking Mountain
chapters.summary: Yara POV. She carries the dying Cael up the true road as the old gods rise through the peaks, and the armies below turn to ash and snowmelt. She bargains with the waking mountain itself, offering her guild's roads as sacred ground. Emotional beat: exhausted awe; inheritance transformed, not lost.

chapters.title: Terms with the Old Gods
chapters.summary: Yara POV. The old gods, newly awake and hungry for worship, want what Vaskal wanted. Yara, the only mortal who has out-bargained two courts, negotiates a covenant: the gods get the mountains' wild places, mortals keep the passes. Emotional beat: triumph with a scar on it.

chapters.title: What Cael Owes
chapters.summary: Cael POV. The gods offer Cael restoration as their first priest; he asks instead for a mortal life beside Yara, debts unpaid. Yara chooses him over the guild's restoration the gods dangle. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved — she chooses the person, not the institution.

chapters.title: The Last Spire
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Spring returns; the guildhall reopens — not as smugglers, but as wardens of the covenant, the guild reborn as something its founders never imagined. Yara hangs Marette's and Brenn's names in the hall. Emotional beat: mourning braided with renewal; inheritance honored by change.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered, Roads Open
chapters.summary: Yara POV, coda. A traveler arrives at the reopened guildhall with an impossible request, and Yara — soul her own, road ahead open, Cael at her side — takes the job. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the story ends where smuggling began, but everything has changed.
